page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.10xlarge is a dedicated compute-and-memory instance belonging to the High Clock Speed instance family. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM virtualization, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance configuration provides 40 vCPUs across 20 physical cores, with two threads per core. Memory capacity is set to 384.0 GB, which corresponds to 9.6 GB of RAM per physical core, placing it firmly in the memory-optimized configuration spectrum.

The CPU includes hardware feature sets such as AVX-512 (with VNNI support), AES cryptography extensions, and bit manipulation instructions (BMI2, ADX, FMA). Cache hierarchy comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Benchmarks reflect balanced mid-range performance, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1277.0 and a multi-core score of 11916.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 34031.19. Memory throughput measures 111.38 GB/sec for large-block reads and 49.57 GB/sec for large-block writes.

Networking performance offers a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating the use of remote network-attached block storage for persistent data. In specialized execution tests, the system achieved 32.74 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 24.49 GB/sec. On CPU-based inference workloads, small 135M language models achieve 78.27 text generation tokens per second, while 7B parameter models produce 12.54 tokens per second.

With its 9.6:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high clock speeds, ecs.hfr6.10xlarge is suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Primary workload fits include large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis, heavy data analytics pipelines, and memory-bound transactional backend systems.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.10xlarge is a memory-optimized, high-clock-speed instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Configured with 40 dedicated vCPUs (20 physical cores) and 384.0 GB of memory, it delivers a high memory allocation of 9.6 GB per physical core. The hardware profile includes AVX-512 extensions and a 35 MB L3 cache, backed by 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying on external block storage volumes for persistent data. Benchmark performance places it in the mid-tier bracket across compute and memory operations, registering 32.74 million Redis SET operations per second and a multi-threaded decompression rate of 164.02 GB/sec. Given its large RAM footprint and dedicated compute resources, ecs.hfr6.10xlarge is well matched for memory-resident databases, caching services, and complex data-processing backends.
